subsystems.name: Chassis organism
subsystems.role: the living platform whose genome is rewritten for space conditions.

subsystems.name: Genetic control circuits
subsystems.role: make the organism do useful work only when and where instructed.

subsystems.name: Metabolic pathways
subsystems.role: the chemistry the cell performs on local materials.

subsystems.name: Bioreactor and growth hardware
subsystems.role: keeps cells alive at low pressure, wide temperature swings and high radiation.

subsystems.name: Containment
subsystems.role: prevents engineered organisms from contaminating a pristine world.

subsystems.name: Product recovery
subsystems.role: extracts metals, gases or materials from the culture.

buildSteps.title: Pick and characterise a chassis
buildSteps.detail: Start from organisms that already tolerate radiation, cold, dryness and salt; sequence and map their genomes.

buildSteps.title: Model the target environment
buildSteps.detail: Recreate Martian or lunar conditions in the lab using regolith simulants, low pressure, UV and perchlorate salts.

buildSteps.title: Design the genome
buildSteps.detail: Use software to plan gene deletions and insertions, then synthesise the DNA chemically.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and edit cells
buildSteps.detail: Insert the circuits with CRISPR-based or other editing tools, and strip out genes that waste energy.

buildSteps.title: Select under stress
buildSteps.detail: Grow the edited strains through many generations under simulated space conditions so useful mutations survive.

buildSteps.title: Prove containment
buildSteps.detail: Test kill switches and nutrient dependence over long periods, since a leak could contaminate another planet.

buildSteps.title: Scale up the culture
buildSteps.detail: Move from millilitre flasks to litre and cubic-metre bioreactors that a mission could actually carry.

buildSteps.title: Test off Earth
buildSteps.detail: Fly strains to the ISS or on a lander to check survival through launch, vacuum and radiation.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into a mission loop
buildSteps.detail: Connect the organism to habitat life support or a mining process, so its output feeds the crew or the machinery.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap, accurate DNA synthesis and genome editing
prerequisites.why: writing whole pathways and trimming genomes is routine in labs on Earth.
naturally tough microbes are known, but engineered ones have not survived years of space radiation.
kill switches work in the lab but have not been shown to hold for decades in an alien environment.

prerequisites.tech: Planetary protection policy and detection methods
prerequisites.why: international rules already restrict what may be sent to Mars and how contamination is measured.
closed-loop systems using algae, bacteria and plants have been tested on the ground and in orbit, not at full scale.
rovers have measured Martian soil chemistry, but mining and processing at useful rates are unproven.

pathway.milestone: lab experiments growing engineered microbes in regolith simulants under simulated space conditions
pathway.unlocks: proof that biology can work on local materials at all.

pathway.milestone: microbes flown to the ISS and returned, showing they survive the space environment
pathway.unlocks: confidence to design a planetary mission around them.

pathway.milestone: robotic demonstration of biomining or waste conversion on the Moon or Mars
pathway.unlocks: real data on yields, contamination and bioreactor survival.

pathway.milestone: engineered organisms embedded in a habitat's air, water and material loops
pathway.unlocks: lighter missions that make fuel, food and metals where they land instead of shipping them.

pathway.milestone: self-sustaining engineered communities supporting long-term settlements
pathway.unlocks: a biology-based industrial base beyond Earth.
